subject: DPA: residency, retention edge-cases and operational exception playbook
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@aurum-systems.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurum Legal <legal@aurum-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPA draft — a few operational questions on retention carve-outs

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending over the latest DPA draft (we've attached our annotated v3). We reviewed the retention & deletion sections and have three areas where we need operational clarification before we can agree the language:

1) Backups and snapshot restores — your DPA currently says "backups retained up to 90 days for disaster recovery" but doesn't clarify whether backups created in EU zones may be restored into a non-EU region in an emergency. We need an explicit constraint or an exception process.

2) Ephemeral telemetry — we want an explicit short window for debug telemetry that references an operational manifest (who can approve a >72hr retention).

3) Proof-of-deletion — for regulated workloads we need a signed manifest for erasure events (including snapshot tombstone times) and an SLA for providing that evidence.

I attached our redlines (Aurum_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can: a) commit to EU-only restores unless a documented and audited escape request is approved, and b) provide a deletion manifest within 10 business days?  

If it's easier, happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the three items.

Best,
Sophie

--
Sophie Grant
Head of Cloud Security, Aurum Systems

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA draft — a few operational questions on retention carve-outs

Sophie — thanks for the clear notes and the redline doc. Short answers up front:

• EU-only restores: yes, by default we enforce EU-only restores for EU-hosted snapshots. We can add explicit language to the DPA that restores will remain in-region except when an "escape approval" is executed via the documented ops playbook and signed by both parties.

• Ephemeral telemetry: we can add a 72-hour telemetry TTL for debug traces and require change control for retention >72h; change control would need a justification, owner, and retention end date.

• Proof-of-deletion: we can provide a signed deletion manifest. We propose a 7-business-day SLA for providing the manifest for routine erasures and 10 business days for snapshot-chain evidence requests.

I pulled the small operational edits into a short playbook (redwood_erase_playbook_v1.pdf) and attached it. Jonas and Marissa are looped in to confirm the operational feasibility and the precise wording for the DPA. Happy to take a call this afternoon if that helps.

Regards,
Laura

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@aurum-systems.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:35:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA draft — a few operational questions on retention carve-outs

Laura / Sophie — quick operational confirmation and suggested redline text we can include in the DPA.

Operational constraints (confirmed):
- Restores: snapshots created in EU zones will be tagged with a region-lock attribute (eu_region_lock=true). Restores to non-EU zones are blocked by default at the orchestration layer. To allow an out-of-region restore we require a documented "Geo-escape Request" submitted in our ticketing system, approval by Redwood CS Ops + Aurum security contact, and an audit log entry containing justification and timestamps.

- Backup TTLs: backups (longer-term archives) are retained per the DPA retention table; short-term rolling snapshots are tombstoned after the configured snapshot TTL. In emergency RTO cases, we will only perform cross-region restores under the Geo-escape Request process.

Suggested DPA clause (plain language):
"Redwood will store, process, and perform routine restores of Customer data within the geographic region/zone specified in Appendix A. Restores of region-locked snapshots to a different geographic region require a documented and auditable Geo-escape Request, signed by an authorized Aurum security representative and Redwood CS Ops. Redwood will maintain an immutable audit trail for any such cross-region activity and will provide proof of the audit trail on request within the SLA specified in Section 4.2."

Proof-of-deletion workflow (practical steps):
1) Customer requests deletion via API or support ticket (include dataset ID).
2) Redwood enqueues deletion job; job emits initial tombstone event.
3) If deletion affects snapshots/backups, Redwood performs tombstone propagation and writes a deletion manifest (sha256 checksums optional) to the customer audit bucket.
4) Redwood provides signed manifest (PDF) via secure link within 7 business days for routine requests; 10 business days for complex snapshot-chain requests.

Marissa — can you confirm we can produce the signed manifest within 7 business days by default and the audit bucket approach?

Thanks,
Jonas

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@aurum-systems.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA draft — a few operational questions on retention carve-outs

Thanks — confirming operational feasibility and a few implementation notes.

1) Signed manifest: we can produce a machine-generated deletion manifest that includes dataset IDs, tombstone timestamps, and a short provenance chain (which snapshot IDs were affected). For signing we will apply Redwood's private key and return a signed PDF. 7 business days is achievable for routine dataset deletions if the request contains the required IDs; for snapshot-chain reconstructions we may need up to 10 business days.

2) Audit bucket & access: the manifest will be written to a customer-specific audit bucket (S3/GCS) with restricted ACLs and retention 30 days to allow customer retrieval. We will include a one-time signed URL in the response.

3) Emergency cross-region restores: operations will attempt an in-region restore first. If a Geo-escape Request is initiated, the ticket will require the Aurum approver's name, rationale, and permitted restore window. We will log the VM/instance and target region in the audit trail.

4) Ephemeral telemetry TTL: we will set default TTL=72h and add a controlled exception workflow; exceptions are rare and require justification plus a retention end-date.

Next steps: Laura, can we add the DPA clause Jonas suggested and an Appendix reference to the erase_playbook? Sophie — if that sounds OK, we'll push a tracked-redline back to your team by EOD tomorrow.

—Marissa

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: DPA draft — a few operational questions on retention carve-outs

Laura / team — this all looks reasonable and addresses our main concerns. A few minor asks before we sign:

• Please include the Geo-escape Request template as Appendix B so our legal team has a form to sign.
• Can you make the provision for the deletion manifest delivery 'within 7 business days' (routine) explicit in the DPA table rather than only in an appendix?
• For the audit bucket retention, could you extend the customer retrieval window to 45 days instead of 30 — gives us more time for cross-team validation.

If you can push the updated DPA with those three edits by end of day tomorrow, I will circulate to Aurum Legal for final sign-off. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sophie
